name: What drain upgrades are needed when converting a tub to a shower?

mainEntity.name: What drain changes are usually required when a bathtub is converted into a shower?
mainEntity.text: What drain changes are usually required when a bathtub is converted into a shower?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drain work is one of the most overlooked parts of a tub-to-shower conversion. A shower typically handles water differently than a tub, so the drain must work with the new pan, slope, and waterproofing system. In some projects, the existing drain can stay in place with a compatible shower base. In others, the drain needs upgrading, repositioning, or complete replacement to prevent slow drainage and standing water. This is especially important in older homes where plumbing may not be sized or vented the way a modern shower expects. Homeowners should ask how the drain will connect to the new pan, whether the shower floor will be sloped properly, and what happens if the existing drain is corroded or off-center. Drain details are not just technical extras; they directly affect performance and leak prevention. A quality conversion should explain the drain plan before the project starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: A shower often needs a larger or better-positioned drain than a tub, along with proper slope and waterproofing around the pan. If the existing drain is undersized, misaligned, or damaged, it may need to be replaced or relocated during the project.
